title: Decision log
description: The frontmatter of decision-log.md at the specification root — «One decision log per specification root, append-only» (SPEC-001 R9). «It is mandatory and non-normative: it constrains nothing; it discloses» (SPEC-003 R5). One append-only list — each entry records a fact the analysis decided rather than read, locating the file and field it filled so a human can evaluate the decision after the fact; a node or field that leaves the specification is answered by an entry retiring its location, never by editing the entry that located it. The log is the only place where agent-decided and material-stated are told apart, and after authoring it is the only index of a node the specification gained by reading a plan's material: that entry carries `found` and no value — «It decides no value and carries no `why`» (SPEC-001 R9) — and a read entry and a decided one are told apart by shape. An empty list is a specification whose material answered everything, and that claim must be true. `field` locates frontmatter and cannot locate a body heading, and that boundary is deliberate: a decision lands in an addressable home — a declared field, a rule's statement, a scenario's case — never in body prose, so a fact whose shape only prose could hold gains a field or a node before it is decided. Prose brought into agreement with a fact a node already states is not a decision and takes no entry; an entry pointing at prose would disclose a decision no validator can re-find.

entries.unstated: The material does not say what shape an evidence value takes.
entries.why: Every evidence sample in the material is shown as free text.

location.description: The file the decision filled, relative to the specification root. Must resolve, unless a later entry retires this location.

field.description: The field the decision filled, dotted from the frontmatter root. Its head must exist in the located file, unless a later entry retires this location.

decided.description: The value the analysis chose. Required with `why` on a decided entry; absent on a read entry, which chose nothing.

found.description: Where material outside the specification root states the fact — the intake path and the sentence — on an entry recorded as read. The path is not resolved: a work root is not the specification's to hold, and this text is what survives when it is gone. Present here, `decided` and `why` are refused: reading chose no value, and an entry carrying both shapes discloses two provenances for one fact.

retired.description: Where the fact an earlier entry located is held now that its node or field left the specification — the node and field that hold it, or that it is held nowhere — on an entry retiring that location. «An entry is never edited or removed» (SPEC-001 R9): the earlier entry stands, and this one is what lets its location stop resolving. Present here, `unstated`, `decided`, `why` and `found` are refused: a retirement discloses where a decision went, and decides and reads nothing. It retires every earlier entry carrying the same `location` and `field`, and one retiring nothing an earlier entry located is refused.

why.description: Why that value — the claim a reviewer can reject; absent on a read entry. One claim: what about the material or the model makes this value the right one, stated so rejecting it is a single disagreement rather than a reading. What does not belong here is the argument that the specification composes — that this node rather than a sibling is the home, that another node's reasoning transfers, that one question keeps one answer. That argument records no decided value, so it has no entry of its own and reaches the log only smuggled into an entry about something else, where it restates the prose of the node the entry locates — «No artifact restates another's statement» (SPEC-001 R7). Its home is the change that made it.
